summary.text: A 39-year-old woman with known papillary thyroid carcinoma, described in the abstract as recurrent, (classic type, pT1N1b) after total thyroidectomy and radioactive iodine therapy presented 5 months after the RAI treatment with upper limb weakness and pain. Cervical spine MRI showed an expansile lytic C6 lesion suspicious for metastasis, and post-RAI therapeutic and diagnostic scans were negative for RAI-avid lesions. Laboratory results showed high stimulated thyroglobulin (145.7), calcium 12.2 mg/dl, PTH 863.7 ng/ml and ALP 417 IU/ml.

A Tc-99m MIBI scan done 8 months later showed persistent right supraclavicular and mediastinal retention suspicious for ectopic parathyroid adenomas, and left wrist pain and swelling prompted an MRI showing a lytic distal ulna lesion suggesting GCT. FDG PET/CT showed an FDG-avid, non-RAI-avid right supraclavicular lymph node, multiple hypermetabolic lytic bone lesions and a non-FDG-avid mediastinal lesion, raising possible ectopic parathyroid mass with brown tumors, with thyroid skeletal metastases not entirely excluded.

A tru-cut biopsy of the right supraclavicular lymph node revealed metastatic thyroid carcinoma, and the patient underwent right neck dissection and mediastinal mass excision. Intra-operative PTH declined from 863.7 to 100 ng/ml. Final histopathology showed the right supraclavicular lymph nodes were metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma and the superior mediastinal mass was a parathyroid adenoma, confirming the provisional PET/CT impression.

Ten months later follow-up FDG PET/CT showed complete metabolic resolution of all the previous FDG-avid skeletal lesions with some sclerotic changes and re-mineralization of the brown tumors. The authors cite the post-surgical decrease in calcium and PTH as supporting the assumption that the lesions were brown tumors rather than bone metastases, without histological proof. No whole-body or SPECT imaging was acquired in the MIBI scan.

ambiguities.issue: The case text calls the nonavid mediastinal lesion a superior mediastinal lesion while the Figure 3 caption calls the non-FDG-avid structure a large anterior mediastinal soft tissue mass.

evidence.quote: Tc-99m MIBI-avid superior mediastinal lesion was non-FDG-avid
non-FDG-avid large anterior mediastinal soft tissue mass (blue arrows)

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not assume the two descriptions are one lesion or two different lesions, and do not merge the two observations.

ambiguities.issue: The abstract describes the case as recurrent papillary thyroid cancer, but the case text gives no recurrence date or disease status for the primary tumor.

evidence.quote: In this case report of recurrent papillary thyroid cancer and ectopic parathyroid adenoma

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not infer when the recurrence occurred or set a disease status for the primary tumor.

ambiguities.issue: The sentence states upper limb weakness and pain without saying whether the pain is also in the upper limb.

evidence.quote: with upper limb weakness and pain

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not assign a body site to the pain.

ambiguities.issue: Thyroglobulin is printed as 145.7 with no unit, and PTH is printed in ng/ml as in the source.

evidence.quote: high stimulated serum thyroglobulin (sTg) level (145.7)
PTH (863.7ng/ml)

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not supply a thyroglobulin unit or convert the printed PTH unit.

ambiguities.issue: The intra-operative PTH sentence begins at 863.7, the same number as the earlier laboratory PTH, but the source does not state that they are the same measurement.

evidence.quote: Intra-operative PTH level declined from 863.7 to 100ng/ml.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not record a second 863.7 measurement or merge it with the earlier laboratory value.

ambiguities.issue: Figures 7 and 8 label preoperative and postoperative images, but the text does not say whether the preoperative images are the same PET/CT study described with Figures 3 to 5.

evidence.quote: A, B (preoperative) images show hypermetabolic left iliac lytic bone lesions (red arrows)
hypermetabolic multiple lytic bone lesions with diffusely increased bone marrow metabolic activity in the axial and peripheral skeleton (Figs. 3, 4, and 5)

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not assume the preoperative images in Figures 7 and 8 are the same study as Figures 3 to 5.

ambiguities.issue: The MIBI scan is dated 8 months later without a named starting point; neither the adjacent laboratory sentence nor the earlier RAI treatment or presentation sentences is named as its anchor.

evidence.quote: A Tc-99m MIBI scan was done 8 months later

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not order the MIBI scan against the laboratory results, RAI treatment or presentation, and do not compute an interval.

ambiguities.issue: The Figure 6 caption describes histology without naming the specimen; the text cites Figure 6 after reporting both the lymph node and the mediastinal mass histopathology.

evidence.quote: Final histopathological examination of the specimen revealed that the right supraclavicular lymph nodes were metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma while the superior mediastinal mass was a parathyroid adenoma confirming the provisional impression of the ^(18)F-FDG PET/CT (Fig. 6)
The overall feature perfectly fits a parathyroid adenoma

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not assign the histology descriptions to a specific specimen beyond the caption conclusion of parathyroid adenoma.

article_limitations: Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; the 8 JPEG figures were inspected in the separate visual target.
Hyperparathyroidism is not stated as a diagnosis of this patient in the case text (only in generic abstract conclusions), so no condition was recorded.
Brown tumors are an imaging-based supposition with no histological proof; they are recorded as possible/provisional.
Thyroglobulin has no printed unit; PTH unit ng/ml is as printed. No flags were derived from reference ranges.
Background paragraphs, literature statistics and generic conclusions are not patient facts.
Table 1 is a summary of imaging findings with assumptive and definitive diagnoses; its cells are cited as evidence of the matching observations and conditions.
No supplementary files are listed for this article.
